negative_controls.details: 14 of 15 negative controls HELD as expected. 1 FAILED (NC-12). NC-12 (planted residue in product-out/) failed because the comparator checks only declared retained_output_refs and does not detect undeclared extra files. This is a documented scope limitation of the comparator-only check, not a product defect. NC-11 sub-reason note: the precommit predicted forbidden_run_status_observed but the actual sub-reason was run_status_mismatch. This is because the observed run_status was clean (not inconclusive), so the forbidden_run_status check did not fire; run_status_mismatch fired instead because the counterfactual expected inconclusive but observed clean. The control still HELD -- the disagree/product_disagreement outcome was correct, only the sub-reason path differed. Additional caveat: the run-negative-control.mjs script used to execute these controls has a SHA-256 (951326f7...) that differs from the oracle precommit's committed digest (a8f0d1b6...), meaning negative controls were run with tooling not bound by the precommit. This weakens the negative control evidence chain, though the tooling-test-result honestly records the actual digest.

candidate_defect_register.details: CDF-001 accurately describes the NC-12 finding: the comparator's retained_output_refs check verifies only declared files and does not detect undeclared extra files planted in the retained workspace tree. The defect is correctly marked severity=informational, affects_verdict=false, affects_claim_ceiling=false. The description is consistent with the NC-12 result file's note field. The resolution correctly characterizes this as a scope limitation of the comparator-only check vs the full offline verification pipeline.

digest_discrepancies.impact: The negative control orchestration script was modified after the oracle precommit was frozen. No precommit amendment was recorded. The tooling-test-result honestly captures the actual digest. This affects the negative control evidence chain but does not affect scenario comparisons (which use the comparator, whose digest is verified). The 14/15 HELD outcome provides compensating evidence that the controls function correctly despite the unrecorded script change.

caveats: run-negative-control.mjs SHA-256 mismatch: the oracle precommit committed to digest a8f0d1b6... but the script on disk (and recorded in tooling-test-result.json) is 951326f7.... The precommit's amendments array is empty, so this change was not formally recorded. This weakens the pre-registration of the negative control tooling, though the controls themselves produced the expected outcomes (14 HELD, 1 documented FAILED).

NC-11 sub-reason path: the precommit predicted forbidden_run_status_observed but the actual mechanism was run_status_mismatch. The control HELD correctly (disagree/product_disagreement) but via a different code path than the precommit anticipated. The NC-11 result note explains this is because the observed status was clean, not inconclusive, so the forbidden_run_status check did not trigger. This is a precommit prediction inaccuracy, not a control failure.

NC-12 FAILED is a known and documented scope limitation of the comparator-only check. CDF-001 in the candidate defect register describes it accurately. The comparator does not guarantee tree-level integrity against extra planted files; the full offline verifier (product code) provides that check.
notes: The four scenario comparisons form the core evidence and are fully verified: all four show agree/product_agreement with complete binding, all expectation digests chain correctly from precommit through comparator, and determinism is confirmed across the first attempt and completion run. The execution lock and oracle precommit form an intact digest chain for the comparator tooling, adapter artifact, and dependency pins. The single digest discrepancy (run-negative-control.mjs) affects the negative control evidence chain only, not the scenario comparisons. The completion declaration correctly characterizes the run as confirmatory (not blind). Overall, the evidence supports admissibility of all four scenarios with the noted caveats.
